title: Remove Settings patch writer flat export
summary: Removed the transitional window.writeSettingsPatchJson flat export and routed Settings Libraries patch staging through window.mediaPipelineSettingsView.writeSettingsPatchJson.
reason: Continue the WebView namespace-first cleanup for the touched Settings domain without restoring compatibility globals or moving settings mutation authority into the frontend.
behavior_before: SettingsView exported writeSettingsPatchJson both through mediaPipelineSettingsView and as window.writeSettingsPatchJson; Settings Libraries called the flat alias when staging LibraryProfiles and watch-folder patches.
behavior_after: SettingsView exposes writeSettingsPatchJson only through mediaPipelineSettingsView. Settings Libraries resolves the Settings namespace once and calls settingsView.writeSettingsPatchJson for staging, while backend Preview/Save remains the authority for persisted settings writes.
tests_added: Added a static guard that settingsView.js keeps writeSettingsPatchJson on mediaPipelineSettingsView without a window.writeSettingsPatchJson flat alias.
Updated Settings Libraries static coverage to require settingsView.writeSettingsPatchJson calls and reject the flat alias.
Corrected stale Settings Libraries review-dialog assertions to the current backend-evidence counter rows.
manual_validation: Clean detached temp worktree at HEAD plus this packet's source/test patch: npm run webview:prework:check passed after regenerating WebView map/contract/slice/check artifacts there.
rollback_plan: Restore window.writeSettingsPatchJson = writeSettingsPatchJson, change Settings Libraries call sites back to window.writeSettingsPatchJson, revert the static assertions, and regenerate the WebView public-contract/split-map/split-candidate artifacts plus generated summaries. This rollback does not touch backend settings persistence, source media, queue state, publish/drain, rename apply, or media policy.
notes: No backend route, strict confirmation, settings persistence, source/scratch/output movement, publish/drain, FFmpeg/media-policy, or command-journal behavior changed. Generated WebView contract files were produced in a clean detached worktree based on HEAD plus only this packet's Settings patch so unrelated rename-generated drift in the dirty main worktree is not absorbed into this packet.
